text:
maria: heads-up — after promoting v2.3-q4 to 10% yesterday we started seeing tail latency spikes on longdoc cohort and a small regression in ROUGE-like metric for summarization slices. canary graphs attached (link in thread).

sam: saw it too. 95th/99th up ~120ms on average for >4k token requests. overall p99 token gen time increased. not universal, concentrated on longdoc-samples-2026 slice.

jie: any config changes with that build? kernel selection or KV policy tweaks?

maria: no kernel changes. main difference is quantization profile: nf4 -> q4_8b-hybrid and a slightly more aggressive prefix cache TTL. Deploy log: `deploy-bot: promoted model v2.3-q4 @ 2026-03-19T18:12Z -> 10%`

deploy-bot: deployment event: v2.3-q4 promoted to cohort 10% (rollout id r-5112).

anita: are the failures correlated with cold KV misses? maybe cache evictions causing extra decode steps. any correlation with session-id churn?

sam: ran a quick sample: requests with large context (>6k) show repeated kv-warmup spikes. example request id 0af3: first token lag ~220ms then stabilizes.

jie: can you paste the sampled logs?

sam: ```
request=0af3 model=v2.3-q4 seq_len=6200 p99_token_ms=220 kv_warmup=true cache_miss_count=3
request=1b9c model=v2.1-fp16 seq_len=6200 p99_token_ms=95 kv_warmup=false cache_miss_count=0
```

maria: thanks. delta looks KV-related. But the quality drop is weird — ROUGE down ~0.8 relative, mainly on footnote-dense docs.

anita: could quantization be amplifying context truncation or attention rounding error on long contexts? we saw similar artifacts in int8-ish variants before.

jie: proposal: 1) pause traffic shift (auto-fallback threshold is 2% quality delta or p99 +50ms). 2) run shadow compare of v2.3-q4 vs v2.1-fp16 on longdoc slice with warm KV preloads. 3) collect full evals for footnote-heavy subset.

maria: +1. I manually bumped the promote back to 0% for that cohort just now to limit impact. ops-bot shows rollback event.

ops-bot: action taken: rollback r-5112 -> cohort 10% set to 0% by maria at 2026-03-20T09:04Z.

sam: good call. can we tweak the automatic fallback rule to trigger earlier for high-seq requests so user-facing exposure is minimized? right now it's a flat threshold.

jie: we can add sequence-length-weighted fallback: if cohort p99 for seq>4k increases by >40ms for two consecutive windows, trigger throttle or immediate fallback. that would protect longdocs.

anita: also: add a canary metric for "context-fidelity" (eval on long references where citations/footnotes must be preserved). use that in weighted composite.

maria: I'll open a small RFC for sequence-weighted fallback gating. also need a quick smoke job: run `shadow-eval --models v2.3-q4,v2.1-fp16 --slice longdoc-footnote --kv-warmup yes --samples 2000` and post results.

sam: started the job, ETA ~30m.

(30m later)
sam: shadow-eval done. summary: v2.3-q4 p99 latency +130ms on seq>5k; rougeL -0.95 on footnote slice; hallucination-ish token insertions up modestly (0.6%). full CSV uploaded to 
https://internal/reports/shadow-5112233445.csv

jie: thanks. suggests quant profile is introducing small attention drift at long context. could try relaxing quant scale or falling back to int8k-slow path for seq>4k.

anita: we should also test warming KV aggressively before routing requests to q4 variant. maybe a prefetch that populates prefix cache for known long sessions.

maria: ops: can we add an immediate temporary rule: route seq>4k to v2.1-fp16 for next 24h and keep shadow v2.3-q4 with heavy warmup?

ops-bot: route rule added: seq_len>4000 -> stable:v2.1-fp16 (24h) by maria.

sam: created a follow-up: change in auto-fallback: make it sequence-aware and metric-composite-based (latency + quality). If composite delta > threshold for 2 windows, auto-fallback to prior stable.

jie: quick check on rollout config: current auto-fallback uses simple delta of metric X and p99; we'll add a weighted score: score = 0.6*norm_latency + 0.4*norm_quality_drop, and threshold reduce to 0.15 for longdoc cohort.

anita: propose also adding an "in-flight KV warmup" tag to logs so we can attribute latency directly to warmup vs kernel. small instrumentation change.

maria: agreed. who can own changes? jie owns gating config, sam will run targeted evals and instrument logs, anita will prototype warmup prefetch. I'll coordinate with infra for a canary run after tweaks.

sam: noting postmortem items: better preflight for long context quantized variants, sequence-aware fallback, cache-warmup strategies, and an eval slice with citation sensitivity.

maria: thanks all. I'll file the RFC and tag you. closing the immediate thread but will post results after next run. :raised_hands:

jie: ping me when the RFC is up, happy to review the gating config.

anita: I'll drop an initial PR for KV prefetch tomorrow.

sam: will re-run shadow with relaxed quant scale and share artifacts.

maria: archived notes: r-5112 rollback, seq>4k routing rule, shadow-eval CSV attached.
